title: Work and money
theme: Shifts, a bad day, overtime, side gigs, debts, payday, and the job that ends or begins.

storylets.title: One in, one out
storylets.note: Two coworkers pass at a work door at shift change. Common, cheap and quiet.

B.desc: a coworker arriving for the next shift

b1: {A} comes out of the work door stretching both arms over {A.his} head.
{A} leaves the workplace at the end of the shift, shoulders slumped, lanyard swinging.
{A} emerges from the work door and blinks at the daylight.
b2: {B.desc} arrives at the door as {A} is coming out. A few words and a clap on the shoulder.
{A} and {B.desc} trade a short report on the step. {B.desc} nods through it.
{A} says something to {B.desc} and points back inside with a thumb.
b3: {B.desc} goes in and the door slides shut on the end of the sentence.
{B.desc} takes over and enters. {A} is already walking away.
{B.desc} steps through the work door, tying an apron as {B.he} goes.

storylets.title: A day gone wrong
storylets.note: Work trouble pressure shows as behavior only. The feeling arrives through a stated line on a call, never as fact.

A.desc: an employed adult after a bad shift

{A} leaves the workplace with the bag half closed and a shoe untied.
{A} exits and does not slow down at the corner.
b2: Anger mark over {A}. {A} stops, puts both hands on {A.his} head, and walks on.
{A} kicks the base of a lamp once. Anger mark over {A}.
{A} turns back toward the door, stops, then keeps walking.
b3: {A} drops onto a bench, elbows on knees. Stays like that.
{A} sits on a bench with the bag held in both arms like a cushion.
{A} takes a bench at the edge of the square and stares at the ground.
b4: {A} takes a call, voice flat. Low, short answers.
{A} picks up a call and listens for a long time before speaking.
{A} answers a call on the bench and presses the heel of one hand to {A.his} eye.

log: Phone, one side: {A} says "He said it in front of everyone. I did not get a word in."
Phone, one side: {A} says "I'm fine. I just need an hour. It was a long one."

storylets.title: Late out of the work door
storylets.note: A long shift runs over. Money pressure eases a little.

b1: {A} comes out of the work door long after dark. The street lamps are on. A last light goes off behind {A.him}.
{A} emerges, jaw set, bag heavy, and locks the door with a key.
{A} leaves late, much later than the other doors on the block, and stretches in the empty street.
b2: {A} orders at the late stall. Asks for the biggest bowl.
{A} reaches the counter and orders without looking up.
{A} joins a short line of other late workers at {place}.
b3: {A} eats in silence at the end stool, spoon and handset both in hand.
{A} finishes the bowl in a minute, then sits and lets the steam rise.
{A} leans against the counter and eats with {A.his} eyes half closed.

storylets.title: Payday at the counter
storylets.note: A little extravagance after pay arrives. Mundane, warm.

b1: {A} orders the dish with the lit sign beside it, the expensive one, and a drink to go with it.
{A} orders two things and a dessert, and counts out the exact coins with a flourish.
{A} reaches the counter and points at the top of the board.
b2: {A} eats with a spoon in each hand, grinning. Note bubble over {A}.
{A} sits with a full tray and a clean handset. Takes {n} minutes to finish.
{A} eats the dessert first. A pleased look at the sky.

storylets.title: Carrying for cash
storylets.note: A second small job after hours. A.job learned through talk.

A.desc: an adult with a second small job

B.desc: someone who pays A for odd work

b1: {A} carries two stacked boxes along the walk, chin on the top one.
{A} lugs a crate through the evening crowd, calling out apologies.
{A} drags a hand truck loaded with sacks, one wheel shrieking.
b2: {A} sets the load down at the shop door and hands over a slip. {B.desc} signs it.
{A} passes the paperwork to {B.desc}, who checks it against the boxes.
{B.desc} takes the slip from {A} and counts the boxes under {B.his} breath.
b3: {B.desc} talks and counts something on the fingers of one hand. {A} nods.
{A} and {B.desc} settle up on the step. A few notes change hands.
{B.desc} gives {A} a short instruction and points to the next shop down.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Same as last week. Six boxes, one night, cash on the step."
Overheard: {B.desc} tells {A}: "You are the only runner who comes back for the second shift."
Overheard: {B.desc} says to {A}: "Pay is on the step, same as before."
Overheard: {A} calls {B.desc} "boss" and gets a laugh.

storylets.title: Thirty until payday
storylets.note: A friend asked for a small loan. Everything is stated, nothing is thought. Chain: wrk.loan-repaid, or it fizzles into a small awkwardness.

B.desc: a friend of A with a little spare

b1: {A} and {B.desc} walk the square together. {A} is quieter than {B.desc} for the whole stretch.
{B.desc} talks the whole walk. {A} says little and checks the clock tower.
{A} and {B.desc} cross to the benches, {A} half a step behind.
b2: On the bench, {A} talks low and rubs a thumb along the strap of a bag. {B.desc} listens, nods once.
{A} says something and looks away. {B.desc} answers with a short sentence and a tilt of the head.
{A} and {B.desc} sit side by side. {A} leans forward, elbows on knees. {B.desc} leans back.
b3: {B.desc} takes out a few notes and gives them to {A}. {A} presses them flat and tucks them in a pocket.
A folded note passes from {B.desc} to {A}. {A} bows, quick, and puts it away.
{B.desc} counts out a few notes and puts them in {A}'s hand. {A} holds the hand shut.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "Thirty, until payday. I swear it is just till payday."
Overheard: {A} asks: "Can you cover the rest of the week? I'll pay you back on the fifteenth."

A.desc: an adult who borrowed from B

B.desc: the friend who lent the money

b1: {A} and {B.desc} reach the counter together. {A} orders for both and pays before {B.desc} can reach.
{A} holds up two fingers at the stall. {B.desc} objects. {A} pays.
{A} steps up first and orders two bowls, pushing {B.desc}'s hand away from the counter.
b2: {A} puts a folded note in {B.desc}'s hand. {B.desc} counts it and gives half back. {A} refuses.
{A} hands over an envelope. {B.desc} weighs it, shrugs, and pockets it.
{A} passes a small stack of notes across the table. {B.desc} nods once and puts them away.
b3: The two eat side by side. {A} points at {B.desc} with a spoon. {B.desc} laughs. Note bubble over both.
{A} and {B.desc} eat in comfortable silence. {B.desc} pushes the pickles toward {A}.
Both heads down over their bowls. A joke goes back and forth without looking up.

log: Overheard: {A} says: "That's the thirty. Thank you for not asking about it."
Overheard: {A} tells {B.desc}: "Square. You can stop pretending you forgot."

storylets.title: A box on the work step
storylets.note: A lost job. The watcher can see the moment only by luck; usually it arrives as hearsay. Chain: wrk.job-hunt, then wrk.found-new-job.

A.desc: an employed adult losing the job

B.desc: a former coworker or boss, at the door

b1: {A} comes out of the work door at an unusual hour, a cardboard box in both arms.
{A} leaves the workplace in the middle of the day, carrying a box that rattles.
{A} exits the work door, box held against {A.his} chest, jacket over the top.
b2: {A} stands on the step with the box and looks up at the sign. Does not move for a minute.
{A} sets the box down on the step, picks it up again, sets it down.
{A} stays at the work door, box at {A.his} feet, a lanyard still around {A.his} neck.
b3: {B.desc} talks briefly to {A}, one hand on {A}'s shoulder. {A} nods and does not look up.
{B.desc} says something short to {A} and goes back in. {A} stays where {A.he} is.
{A} and {B.desc} exchange a few words at the door. A handshake. The door slides shut on {B.desc}.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says "Nothing personal. It came from above." {A} nods.
Overheard: {B.desc} tells {A}: "I will give you a reference. Come by Friday for the paperwork."

lines: Overheard: {S} tells {L} that {A.desc} got let go last week, "out of nowhere."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} lost the job on a Friday and has been around the block ever since.
Overheard: {S} says to {L}: "You heard? {A.desc} is out of work. They cut a whole shift."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} was let go at the end of last month. {S} mentions the box on the step.
entry: Lost the job a week ago (overheard: a neighbor, in conversation).
Was let go from work last month, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).
Left the workplace for good, said {S} (overheard).

storylets.title: Reading the boards
storylets.note: After a job loss: boards, shop doors, a stall conversation. The jobless pressure shows as time spent in the square.

A.desc: an unemployed adult looking for work

b1: {A} stops at a board by the crossing and reads each card, in order. Copies one onto a handset.
{A} reads the notices pinned to a pole, one finger moving down the list.
{A} reads a card by the shop door twice. Photographs it.
b2: {A} straightens {A.his} jacket and goes in through the shop door.
{A} takes a breath and enters the shop. The door slides shut.
{A} goes in at the shop door, folded paper in hand.
b3: {A} comes out ten minutes later. Shakes {A.his} head to no one in particular.
{A} emerges with the same paper still in hand and heads for the next shop.
{A} leaves the shop at a measured pace and does not look back at it.

storylets.title: A new door to use
storylets.note: The job hunt ends. Usually unwatched; arrives through gossip. Sets a flag so a new-uniform storylet can show it.

A.desc: an unemployed adult who finds a job

B.desc: the new boss at the door

b1: {A} walks to the work block in a pressed shirt and clean shoes, a new lanyard still in its plastic.
{A} crosses the street at the signal, hair combed flat, and checks the number over the door.
{A} walks the block at a measured pace and adjusts a collar on the way.
b2: {B.desc} meets {A} at the door and shakes {A.his} hand. A longer handshake than the others today.
{A} and {B.desc} stand at the door while {B.desc} points up and down the block, one finger tracing a route.
{B.desc} gives {A} a card and a key and says something short.
b3: {A} follows {B.desc} through the work door. It closes.
{B.desc} holds the door and {A} goes in ahead.
{A} and {B.desc} go in. The door slides shut.

log: Overheard: {B.desc} says: "Welcome. First shift Monday. You have the night counter."
Overheard: {B.desc} tells {A}: "Uniform's in the back. Badge by Friday."

lines: Overheard: {S} tells {L} that {A.desc} landed something, "a night counter, I think."
Overheard: {S} says {A.desc} started a new job on Monday and has been out of the house early.
Overheard: {S} says: "{A.desc} found work at last. A real contract, not odd days."
Overheard: {S} mentions that {A.desc} "finally got hired somewhere."
entry: Started a new job recently (overheard: a friend, in conversation).
Found work after weeks of looking, said {S} (overheard).
Was hired last week, per {S} (overheard, in conversation).

storylets.title: A badge no one has seen
storylets.note: Seen after a job change: a new uniform and a verified job from the badge.

A.desc: an adult in a new job

b1: {A} walks in a stiff new jacket, the creases still showing from the pack.
{A} walks to work in a different uniform than before. The badge catches the light.
{A} crosses the street in clothes that do not match any shape {A.he} wore before.
b2: {A} reaches the door and goes in under a new sign.
{A} stops at an unfamiliar door, checks the number, and enters.
{A} steps through the door. It slides shut behind {A}.

log: Badge on the new jacket reads: {A.job}.
Name tag at the work door: {A.job}.
Sign over the new door: {A.employer}.
Door plaque at the new workplace: {A.employer}.

storylets.title: A quiet counter
storylets.note: A keeper with no customers. Money pressure and nothing else. A shrug and an early close.

A.desc: a stall keeper on a slow night

b1: {A} stirs a pot no one has asked for. The square in front of the counter is empty.
{A} wipes the same corner of the counter for the third time.
{A} stands behind the counter with the ladle upright, facing the dark square.
b2: {A} leans on the counter and watches the rain, one elbow on each side of the pot.
{A} stays still. A single customer walks past without slowing.
{A} stands at the counter edge with arms folded. Dots bubble over {A}.
b3: {A} shrugs at no one and starts putting the ladles away an hour early.
{A} gives a slow shake of the head, switches off half the lights, and sits down on the stool.
{A} lifts both hands, palms up, toward the empty plaza.

Both through the work door. The door slides shut.
{B.desc} holds the door and gestures {A} through with a sweep of the arm.

log: Overheard: {A} calls {B.desc} "boss" twice.
Overheard: {B.desc} says to {A}: "I'm coming by every shift this week. Be ready."
